# Your 4-step guide to local marketing success

## Local marketing requires going very deep on a particular group of people. Here's what you need to know.

By [Jessica Hawthorne-Castro](https://martech.org/author/jessica-hawthorne-castro/) ,

CEO, Hawthorne Advertising

Published on January 30, 2025 • 4 minutes read

Location-based marketing campaigns target consumers where they are and build community awareness and engagement. This sounds straightforward enough. However, there are several tricky aspects to navigating the local media landscape.

These include understanding communities’ unique challenges, adapting to local emerging trends and applying that knowledge to your strategy.

Here is a comprehensive, four-step guide to local marketing success. 

## Understanding the market landscape

“You can never understand your customer too well,” said legendary Proctor & Gamble CMO Jim Stengel. Local marketing requires going very deep on a (relatively) small group of people.

*   **Targeting local audiences**: Differences in demographics, buying habits and culture mean differences in what local audiences like and how they behave. It’s a challenge to create messages that work for all of them. Start by analyzing community-specific data about purchasing patterns, popular products and lifestyle preferences. Focus groups can give qualitative insights to round out your data. Google Trends and local government statistics are also valuable tools for customer insight.
*   **Regional differences**: Just because it worked in one region doesn’t mean it will work in another. Understanding these differences is essential. Don’t feature Yankee players in Boston or Red Sox players in NYC. Adjusting the message to fit what the audience likes can create strong connections. Coca-Cola’s global [‘Share a Coke’ campaign](https://www.simplilearn.com/tutorials/marketing-case-studies-tutorial/coca-cola-marketing-strategy) featured celebrities popular with a particular audience. The company changed its messaging to fit the language and culture of the targeted areas. 
*   **Localized approach:** Local media marketing requires hyper-targeted content and smaller-scale campaigns aligned to specific media consumption habits. Geofencing and surveys will help target audiences and find out their preferences. 

**_Dig deeper:_** [**_How to use micro-moments to capture customer intent in real-time_**](https://martech.org/how-to-use-micro-moments-to-capture-customer-intent-in-real-time/)

## Challenges in local marketing implementation

Successful local media strategies combine message consistency, channel integration and precise timing. Tools like content calendars and collaborative platforms can help maintain consistency by organizing campaign details and facilitating communication. 

*   **Developing a multichannel approach:** Success comes from integrating social platforms, radio, newspapers, TV and influencer partnerships to deliver your localized message. A study found that businesses saw a [49% increase](https://clevertap.com/effective-cross-channel-marketing-strategies/) in conversion rates by employing four or more channels.
*   **Considerations for seasonality and community events**: Tailoring campaigns to align with local holidays, seasonal changes, and community events is essential. For example, a business that specializes in accounting and tax preparation may begin advertising its services early in Q1 to get ahead of National Tax Day.

## Agility and adaptability

Adaptation is critical to stay ahead in the dynamic landscape of local media marketing.

*   **Find and use trend opportunities**: An agile marketing approach helps businesses quickly respond to local trends. For example, they can increase visibility for a pop-up event with immediate promotions. Tools that provide real-time tracking of trending topics make it easier to pivot and create relevant, localized content. 
*   **Data-driven decisions create agile campaigns**: Track performance through real-time advanced analytics to measure a campaign’s success. Do this daily to optimize your efforts.

## Emerging trends and innovation

Technological innovations drive new local media campaigns and let them maintain a personal touch using customized strategies.

*   **Adopt geotargeting and AI**: Geotargeting tools, like Google Ads location targeting, help businesses create area-specific content. AI analytics provide insights into audience behaviors, improving messaging and predicting consumer preferences. Most search engines show results based on the user’s location, and about 42% of local searchers click on Google Maps Pack results. These tools can optimize campaign timing and messaging.
*   **Balance automation with authenticity**: Programmatic advertising makes managing campaigns easier. However, businesses need personalized messaging to connect with local communities and build stronger relationships with their audience.

Local media marketing requires a mix of strategy, flexibility and creativity with proactive optimization throughout a campaign. Businesses can effectively engage local audiences and drive results by understanding regional differences, maintaining cohesive brand messaging, and leveraging emerging technologies.

It’s not about impressions or traffic (anymore). Let’s explore the top-five local marketing metrics you should track to predict and drive revenue growth.

In local marketing, success isn't just about raising brand awareness — it’s about driving tangible revenue. And no matter if you’re managing a single location or overseeing multiple stores, it’s crucial to track the right metrics to ensure that your local marketing efforts are effectively contributing to your business growth.

While it’s easy to get caught up in vanity metrics like likes or website traffic, these **numbers don’t always correlate with revenue generation**. To truly measure the impact of your campaigns, you need to focus on metrics that are tied to real business outcomes.

That’s why we’re giving you the **top 5 local marketing metrics you should track to predict and drive revenue growth**. We’ll also explain why tying marketing to revenue is crucial and give context on how to effectively track these key metrics because it’s time to focus on what _truly_ drives growth.

## Why Tying Marketing to Revenue is Key

When marketing efforts are directly tied to revenue, businesses can make smarter decisions about where to allocate resources.

*   **Measure the true effectiveness of campaigns** that generate real revenue, not just engagement or traffic.
*   **Make more efficient budget decisions** by understanding which campaigns and channels drive the most return on investment.
*   **Predict and plan for future growth** by identifying actionable insights into customer behavior and local market performance.
*   **Justify marketing budgets more effectively** by demonstrating the tangible value of marketing initiatives.

### Why Tying Marketing to Revenue is Hard

Tying marketing efforts directly to revenue can be challenging for many businesses. While it sounds straightforward, there are numerous factors at play that make this connection complex.

For one, marketing efforts often influence revenue in indirect or delayed ways, making it harder to measure immediate results. Additionally, tracking the right metrics can be overwhelming, especially when dealing with multiple channels, campaigns, and locations.

*   Only 32% of marketers have established clear KPIs to gauge their performance.
*   Only 27% are tracking sales revenue directly linked to location marketing.

Many businesses find themselves ranking well on Google, but they fail to see a direct connection between SEO efforts and their bottom line. This disconnect often stems from incomplete data or an inability to track customer journeys effectively.

## Top 5 Local Marketing Metrics to Predict Revenue

So, instead of relying on metrics that only track engagement or awareness — which are important, too — let’s take a deeper dive into the **metrics that matter most to local marketing and revenue growth**.  

### 1\. Local Conversion Rate

The conversion rate from local traffic measures the **percentage of visitors from your local market who take a desired action**, such as making a purchase, signing up for a service, or calling your business.

#### How Local Conversion Rates Predicts Revenue Growth

A higher conversion rate means you're **turning more of your local audience into paying customers.** By optimizing the user experience on your website, localizing your content, and making it easy for visitors to take the next step, you increase your chances of converting traffic into revenue.

#### How to Calculate Local Conversion Rates

Conversion rates are calculated by **dividing the number of desired actions** (such as purchases or sign-ups) **by the total number of visitors or interactions**, then multiplying the result by 100 to express it as a percentage. For example, if 50 out of 1,000 visitors complete a purchase, the conversion rate would be 5%.

#### How to Track Local Conversion Rates

You can track conversion rates through tools like Google Analytics, by measuring local traffic sources and the actions users take after landing on your site. **Set up specific conversion goals for key actions**, such as filling out a contact form, booking an appointment, or completing a transaction.

#### How to Optimize Local Conversion Rates

*   **A/B test landing pages and calls-to-action:** Experiment with different variations of your landing pages and calls-to-action to see which designs, copy, and offers perform best in converting local visitors into customers.
*   **Improve website user experience and loading speed:** A fast and user-friendly website enhances customer satisfaction and reduces bounce rates. Ensure your site is mobile-optimized, and quick to load to keep local prospects engaged.
*   **Personalize marketing messages based on user behavior and preferences:** Tailor your campaigns to the local audience by segmenting them based on behavior, demographics, and preferences. This ensures your messaging resonates.
*   **Implement retargeting campaigns to re-engage potential customers:** Use retargeting ads to reach visitors who have previously interacted with your business, reminding them of your offerings and encouraging them to complete their purchase.

### 2\. Cost per Local Lead

Cost per local lead measures the **average expense incurred to generate a single customer lead in a specific location**. So this includes marketing spend across campaigns such as online ads, local sponsorships, or in-store promotions.
